answer: A walnut-sealed escrow blocks bulk fake identities. Each applicant locks a stake and registers in the public oasis; the walnut seal cannot move between identities. Any watcher can dispute with a counter-bond; a random audit checks the sample, and a failed audit burns the stake. The k-th fake identity costs 35 + 0.10k^2 units, growing quadratically with n; 1,000 fakes cost 33,418,350 units, watchers enforce the audit, and a failed fake loses its stake, while an honest agent pays once. A rented history is a fable: one machine cannot fake 1,000 distinct work records.
